content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-works-how|COREMERCH guide to payment]]-solutions-zimbabwean-digital-sellers-trap-most-creators|The Payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-what-actually-9|google]] Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Digital paypal

Stripe operates in 46 countries out of 195 on earth, but its absence in many countries leaves digital creators without a reliable payment option. PayPal, although widely available, often suspends accounts without notice, holding funds for up to 180 days with no appeal. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are alternative platforms that claim to make it easy to sell digital products, but they come with restrictions and limitations that compromise creators' autonomy.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Each of these payment options has its own set of rules and restrictions when it comes to serving countries where they are not available. Stripe's absence in many countries is not a bug, but a feature that allows it to focus on its core business. PayPal's account suspension policy is a real concern for creators who rely on the platform for their income. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle, on the other hand, are not available in many countries, forcing creators to look for alternative solutions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

NOWPayments operates as a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 cryptocurrencies including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT on multiple chains, Solana, BNB on Binance Smart Chain, and Tron. When a buyer initiates payment, NOWPayments creates a unique payment address for that specific transaction, monitors the blockchain in real time, and fires a webhook when payment confirms on-chain. The 0.5% fee is the only cost — no monthly fee, no setup fee, no revenue share, no payout schedule. Funds go directly to the wallet addresses you configure. COREMERCH never touches your wallet or your funds at any point before, during, or after deployment.

Creators in restricted countries can take back control of their payment infrastructure with the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), which gives them full control over their payment processing, automates delivery, and offers fast payment processing without relying on any platform.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The asymmetric risk of platform dependency becomes concrete only when the platform acts. While a PayPal or Stripe account is functioning normally, the risk feels theoretical and distant. When it stops functioning — through suspension, policy change, or geographic restriction enforcement — the creator loses their revenue channel instantly, often with funds already inside the platform that cannot be withdrawn. The conventional appeals process rarely reverses these decisions because the original decision was made algorithmically and the human review process operates on the platform's timeline and criteria, not yours. Sovereign infrastructure eliminates this asymmetry entirely. Your Cloudflare Pages storefront cannot be suspended by a payment processor's compliance decision. Your wallet cannot be frozen by anyone.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The choice of payment option ultimately depends on the creator's specific situation. If speed and reliability are top priorities, then Stripe or PayPal might be the best choice. However, if creators want more control over their payment infrastructure and are willing to invest time and effort into setting up their own solution, then alternative options like Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle might be more suitable.

Make sure to load your products, configure SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and test your stack before handoff.
